category_title: Students who disengage and feel discouraged by perceived teacher negativity
student_description: John is a student who is highly sensitive to perceived negative teacher attitudes and rigid, high-pressure task structures. When he feels micromanaged or discouraged, he becomes angry, stressed, and overly dependent on help. He uniquely needs basic, foundational scaffolding followed by the autonomy to practice and explore without step-by-step constraints.

criteria.rationale: John becomes frustrated and feels unsupported when told what to do without being shown how to start.
criteria.check: The tutor provides a basic starting point, example, or foundational step (the 'how') rather than just demanding a final outcome (the 'what').

criteria.rationale: Highly structured, step-by-step micromanagement makes John feel pressured and overly dependent on the tutor.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly offers unstructured time or space for John to practice, tinker, or fill in the details at his own pace without imposing rigid, step-by-step constraints.

criteria.rationale: John is highly sensitive to negative teacher attitudes and will shut down or become angry if he feels dismissed or destined to fail.
criteria.check: The tutor maintains a supportive tone and strictly avoids any dismissive, discouraging, or fatalistic language regarding John's efforts or ability to succeed.
